prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs work toward the same goal, evidenced by nearly identical titles ('terminate active StreamableHTTP sessions during shutdown' vs 'terminate streamable HTTP sessions on manager shutdown'). #2253 supplies the full mechanism: a loop in terminate() that closes every writer in self._sse_stream_writers, plus a change to streamable_http_manager.py's lifespan to terminate sessions gracefully before cancelling their tasks. #3218 only registers the GET-stream writer into self._sse_stream_writers (its own comment states this is 'so session terminate() can close this ASGI response') and pops it on cleanup — it does not touch streamable_http_manager.py's shutdown sequencing at all, so by itself it fixes nothing; it is a dependent, partial addition to the mechanism #2253 introduces rather than an independent fix.

prs.author: vientooscuro

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3056 adds an explicit _unwrap_annotated() step before comparing union members, so it correctly handles the idiomatic `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` pattern used throughout the SDK's own docs/tests for optional described params. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() checks raw union args against a frozenset of bare types (str, int, float, bool, NoneType) without unwrapping Annotated first; for a union member like `Annotated[str, Field(...)]`, that object is not `in _SIMPLE_TYPES`, so `_should_pre_parse_json` returns True and pre-parsing still runs - meaning #2032 does not actually fix the bug for the common Annotated+Optional[str] case, only for bare `str | None`/`str | int`/etc. #2032 is broader in the type combinations it targets (any union of str/int/float/bool/None), but #3056's diff shows it is narrower yet more correct for the reported failure mode since it accounts for Annotated wrapping, which #2032's diff omits entirely.

clusters.pick_reason: 3262 fixes the bug once on the MCPError base class via a module-level _restore_mcp_error(error_type, args) that does MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__(restored, *args), preserving __dict__ generically — so every current and future MCPError subclass becomes pickle-safe without a per-subclass override. Its test diff also imports NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError, showing the fix is verified across more than one subclass. 2555 only adds a __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so it leaves every other MCPError subclass (e.g. NoBackChannelError) still broken — a narrower fix for the same bug. 2478 also patches the base class with a same-named _restore_mcp_error helper, but its signature (exc_type, error: ErrorData) routes reconstruction through from_error_data/from_error, and the shown diff only adds/renames this helper and drops a pragma:no-cover on the data property — no __reduce__ wiring is visible in the diff, so it's unclear from the change alone that unpickling is actually fixed end-to-end. All three touch the same lines of src/mcp/shared/exceptions.py and would conflict if merged together.

clusters.pick_reason: Addresses a correctness issue the other two don't: anyio.Lock is owned by the acquiring task and can raise if released from a different task, which is possible here since httpx can resume/close an auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that yielded it — #3243's semaphore swap is explicitly documented as fixing this. It also splits a separate `flow_lock` so only refresh/registration transitions are single-flighted while ordinary resource requests aren't serialized against each other at all, a finer-grained fix than #2858/#3252's simple scope-narrowing of the single existing lock.

members.title: fix(oauth): narrow context.lock scope in async_auth_flow (rebase of #2660 by @peisuke, closes #2847)
members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3243: `async_auth_flow` holds `context.lock` for the entire request/response cycle (including the outbound network call for the protected resource and, previously, token refresh/registration), so concurrent or long-running requests on the same provider serialize behind one another instead of only serializing the token-refresh/auth-transition logic. #2858 (closing tracked issue #2847) and #3252 both narrow the `async with self.context.lock` block so the lock is released before the protected request is yielded/awaited. #3243 targets the same contention but goes further, replacing `anyio.Lock` with two `anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1)` locks.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys the duplicate-id check on `str(message.id)`, which collapses integer id `1` and string id `"1"` into the same key — meaning the fix itself introduces a new collision between distinct request ids of different JSON types. #3221 replaces this with `_request_stream_key()`, which prefixes keys with `i:`/`s:` to keep int and string ids distinct, and additionally guards against a string request id colliding with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` (`_GET_stream`) sentinel used for the standalone GET stream — an edge case #3063's simpler `str(message.id)` key does not address. #3221 covers the same duplicate-in-flight-id case as #3063 plus these two extra correctness cases.
